meta.thesis: SpeedCubeShop does not need more cube SKUs - it needs non-cubers to feel the addiction of a first solve, and the 2-Minute Challenge turns a $12 cube into a challenge nobody walks past.
meta.variant_angle: challenge-mechanic retail campaign + judge demo prop

business_problem: SpeedCubeShop sells to people who already cube: the 500-review base is passionate (77% five-star) but self-selected - shipping and first-time quality complaints are the friction (23 one-star), and there is no mechanism to convert 'I can't solve that' curiosity into a first purchase [R1][R3][S2][S5].

objectives.text: Drive 250 attributed orders (challenge-booth QR + online code SOLVE2) in 45 days at ~$24 AOV
Capture 800 email/SMS signups via 2-Minute Challenge booths and solve-tutorial funnels
Reach 1.2M Texas impressions and shift 'cubes are for nerds/kids' to 'the 2-minute challenge anyone tries' - +12 pts among surveyed shoppers

segments.name: Challenge Gamers (13-24)
segments.psychographic: competitive, TikTok-native, can't walk past an unsolved cube
segments.behavioral: impulse buys <$30, shares challenge videos, attends pop-ups
segments.media: TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Instagram, campus/mall foot traffic

methods.recruitment: 500 public Judge.me reviews on speedcubeshop.com, keyword-coded (collected 2026-11-07)
SpeedCubeShop product/pricing pages, starter bundles, social bios vs Amazon toy aisle
Intercept survey at challenge booths, pre vs post campaign

findings.finding: 77% five-star across 500 reviews - the community loves the shop; the product is not the problem
One-star complaints concentrate on shipping delays ('it hasn't came yet') and post-purchase quality drops - the friction is the last mile, same as every DTC retailer
Reviewers are self-identified cubers - almost nobody describes buying a FIRST cube; the challenge-to-purchase gap has no bridge
Speedcubing content is huge on TikTok/YouTube (comps, solves, ASMR) while the retail side markets like a spec shop - the hobby content and the store funnel are disconnected

assumptions.text: $5,000 paid social at ~$7 CPM = ~700K impressions + ~500K organic challenge content
8 challenge-booth shifts at ~$300 each (table, timer, cube stock, signage)
SOLVE2 code: $3 off starter cube; manufacturer-funded, netted in revenue
Accessory repeat purchase ~25% within 90 days (lube, upgrades)

programs.name: 2-Minute Challenge Booths
programs.mechanic: Pop-up challenge stations: solved cube in 2 minutes wins a sticker + $3-off QR; everyone who tries gets captured. The judge prop IS the program.

programs.name: Solve School
programs.mechanic: Beginner solve-tutorial funnel: QR -> 6-step video series -> starter bundle offer. Turns 'I can't' into first purchase.

programs.name: Cube Community Nights
programs.mechanic: Monthly cubing meetup + WCA-competition outreach: the community that already loves the shop becomes the volunteer demo crew.

programs.name: First Cube Friday
programs.mechanic: Weekly drop: starter bundle + beginner solve card at $19.99; SMS/email push each Friday.

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: the shop sells to people who already cube - 77% five-star fans, but no bridge from 'I can't solve that' curiosity to a first purchase [R1][R3].
Solution: the 2-Minute Challenge - booths that dare you to solve it, solve-school funnels, community nights, and weekly first-cube drops.
45-day goal: 250 orders, 800 captures, +12 pts 'anyone can try' [O1-O3].
slides.notes: We don't sell cubes - we dare people to try.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Speed cubes: magnetic, corner-cutting puzzles $5-300+; starter cubes $12-20 with lubes/mats/accessories [S1].
The demo is the product: nobody puts a scrambled cube down without trying it.
Reviews: 77% five-star of 500 - community-loved [R1].
Sold DTC online; no physical retail presence to demo in.
slides.notes: Hold the cube while describing the mechanism - judges feel the magnetic click.

slides.title: Company & Position
bullets: Independent US speedcubing retailer - the hobby's specialist shop vs Amazon's toy aisle [S1][S5].
Speedcubing is booming: WCA competitions, TikTok solve content, ASMR niche - but the retail funnel markets to insiders only [S3][S4][R4].
Positioning gap: 'for cubers' is earned; 'for everyone who can't resist a challenge' is unclaimed.
The campaign claims the challenge side of the brand.

P1 is the growth unlock; P2 is the revenue base.

bullets: Content analysis of 500 public Judge.me reviews (collected 2026-11-07), keyword-coded [R1-R4].
Digital shelf audit of 8 sources: catalog, starter bundles, social vs Amazon positioning [S1][S5].
Pending: intercept survey (n=150) at booths + 3 interviews - field kit ready.
500 reviews is a real corpus; shipping/quality themes are clear.
slides.notes: Biggest corpus yet for a non-food brand.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: [R1] 77% five-star, community-loved -> sell belonging + challenge, not product fixes.
[R2] Complaints are shipping/quality friction -> set expectations at booth + bundle for first-timers, not returns.
[R3] Nobody describes a FIRST cube -> build the bridge: 2-minute challenge = try before you buy.
[R4] Hobby content is massive, store funnel is insider -> Solve School connects viral cubing content to a starter offer.
slides.notes: Every program maps to a finding.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Theme: 2-Minute Challenge - dare them to solve it, then sell them the cube.
Push-pull: booths create the try (pull); retargeting + Friday drops convert later (push) [R3][A4].
Community as crew: cubers staff the booths - authentic demos, zero talent cost [R1].
PESO: paid geo-social, earned comp/community PR, shared challenge clips, owned email/SMS + solve series.

slides.title: Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $9,300: paid social $5K [A4]; creators $2.4K [A6]; booths $2.4K [A7]; production $500 [A10]; contingency ~12% [A11].
Funnel: 1.2M impressions x 2.8% CTR x 0.75% purchase = ~250 orders = $6K revenue [A1][A4].
GP 40% = $2.4K; direct ROI ~-74% - a market-entry proof budget: 800 captures + community activation, payback via accessories repeat (25% within 90 days) [A2][A13].
Honest read: we're buying first-time cubers, not this quarter's margin [A15].

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: SpeedCubeShop owns the inside of the hobby; the outside - everyone who can't resist a scrambled cube - is unclaimed.
The 2-Minute Challenge turns retail into a dare; the dare is the demo; the demo is the sale.
Put a timer and a cube in front of anyone and the thesis proves itself - including in this room.
